_comment: Ground truth for the eval harness: what was ACTUALLY said in each recording.
transcripts.json sits alongside this file and holds what Handy 0.9.6 produced,
errors included. That is the baseline to beat, not the target. Do not conflate them.
References are reconstructed from the session in which the samples were recorded,
including the speaker's own typed corrections -- they explicitly confirmed the
intended words were 'set' and 'reset', which Handy's fuzzy matcher had turned into
'sed' and 'rust'. Every entry is "verified": false until someone listens to the
audio and confirms it. Do not report WER from unverified references as fact.
'exercises' names the specific failure each sample probes, so a regression can be

samples.reference: So, this is a test. Let's try some commands here. Let's make a dir with the command mkdir named test and touch a new file test_file and then rm -rf this whole folder again.
exercises: commands -> comments: technical word lost to a common English neighbour
a dir -> there: context error, hotword biasing cannot fix this
mkdir -> MK D I R / mkir: fixed by hotwords at score 1.5
rm -rf -> RMRF: command name run together
test_file -> test underscore file: spoken punctuation not symbolised
Very short utterance. Primary check that pre-roll keeps the first word:
at 1.3s there is no room to lose the leading 'cd' and still score.

samples.reference: I have udev rules, udev rules to set the keyboard layout, but I think something you did reset it.
exercises: set -> sed and reset -> rust: the fuzzy-replacement regression this project bans.
The speaker confirmed both intended words in writing.
MUST still decode 'set' and 'reset' correctly even with 'sed' in the vocabulary.
This is the guard test for text.replacements staying exact-match.
THE REGRESSION SAMPLE. Handy produced an empty transcript for this clip:
'Timed out waiting 30s for live transcription to finalize'. 37s of speech,
silently discarded.
Spoken content is unrecovered, so this cannot be scored for accuracy. It is
still the most important sample in the set: a one-shot decode MUST return
non-empty text well inside the clip's own duration. Assert that, not WER.

samples.reference: Okay, we are now at the new model. The overlay is there but not wide enough. And okay, let's see the text quality. But I think the whole system is not great, so maybe before we build our own we should uninstall and reset everything and then try a structured approach to write a plan and then build it.
exercises: Near-clean prose: the speaker rated this decode's quality good.
Only known error is 'system' -> 'systemd'. Useful as an upper baseline --
if hotword biasing degrades this sample, hotwords_score is too high.
Also over 25s, so it is a second guard against any streaming-style time cap.
